newsitem.title: USA: Boeing official doubtful of TWA fuel-tank theory.
newsitem.headline: Boeing official doubtful of TWA fuel-tank theory.

text.p: A top Boeing Co official expressed doubts Monday that fuel-tank design may have contributed to the crash of Trans World Airways Boeing 747 in the Atlantic off New York on July 17.
"I do not believe that we have a problem out there in the fleet," said Stephen Hatch, Boeing's chief project engineer.
"We have 8,000 Boeing plans out there. There are 14,000 airplanes that are in the fleet worldwide for all commercial aircraft worldwide," he said on ABC's "Good Morning America."
Hatch did say the aircraft maker would be willing to do whatever is needed to improve safety. "Anytime we can improve the margin of safety, it's in all of our interests."

Last Friday, the Federal Aviation Administration said it would issue an order this week to inspect wing fuel pump wiring on some early Boeing 747 aircraft. The agency said the potential wiring problem was uncovered during the investigation of the TWA crash.
However the FAA said it had no evidence to link the wiring to the crash.

In a written statement to the FAA last week, the National Transportation Safety Board recommended modifications to aircraft design to prevent fuel tank explosions. The FAA said it would urgently review the board's request.
On Friday, Boeing said it was reviewing the recommendations announced by the NTSB regarding proposed changes to the company's 747-type aircraft.
A spokesman for the Seattle-based aircraft maker said at the time it would comply with the recommendations if the FAA decides to enforce them.
